newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Mob attacks Indonesia's Golkar party supporters.
newsitem.headline: Mob attacks Indonesia's Golkar party supporters.

text.p: Supporters of Indonesia's ruling Golkar party were attacked by a stone-throwing mob while campaigning for general elections, and at least 12 people were injured, the official Antara news agency said on Friday.

The news agency said a convoy of vehicles carrying Golkar supporters was attacked by an unidentified group of people in the town of Malang in East Java province on Thursday, leading to several incidents in which the 12 people were injured.
Sporadic violence has broken out over Indonesia's main Java island in the past few days as the campaign for the May 29 general elections entered its last week. The campaign ends on May 23.
Golkar is expected to win easily, but the minority Moslem-based United Development Party (PPP) has been attracting large crowds to its campaign rallies.
The third party legally allowed to contest, the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI), is likely to be routed, analysts have predicted.
Newspapers said at least 10 other political party supporters were injured on Thursday, including three who were stabbed.
The Jakarta Post newspaper reported that P.M. Imron, leader of the PPP branch in Temanggung, Central Java, was seriously injured by masked men who stabbed and beat him.

"Police have told us the stabbing will be investigated. We do not plan to hold any campaign until Tuesday in protest against the incident and Imron is still being treated in hospital," a PPP official told Reuters by telephone from Temanggung.

The hilly town of Temanggung, 400 km (250 miles) southeast of Jakarta, has been rocked by violent clashes involving PPP and Golkar supporters in the past few weeks. The PPP official said Golkar did not campaign in Temanggung on Thursday for fear of violence.

Clashes also erupted in Pasuruan, in East Java, on Thursday between PPP and Golkar supporters, Republika newspaper reported. At least two people were stabbed during the clash which started after PPP supporters threw stones at a Golkar convoy.
In Jakarta, several people were injured in a clash on Thursday between Golkar supporters and construction site workers who refused to join them in shouting slogans.

Golkar, in power for the last 30 years under President Suharto, is seeking to push its share of the vote to more than 70 percent from the 68 percent it won at the last polls in 1992. The PPP won 17 percent and the PDI 15 percent.
